The therapist gave her a neck massage.

easy.def: Very big and heavy.
examples: The elephant is massive.
The rock is massive.
A massive tree fell.

more.def: Very large, heavy and solid.
examples: The massive rock blocked the road.
A massive tree stood in the park.
The elephant is a massive animal.

easy.def: The tall pole on a ship that holds the sails.
examples: The sail is on the mast.
A sailor climbed the mast.
The mast is tall.

more.def: A tall pole on a ship that holds up the sails and flags.
examples: The sailor climbed the mast to look out for land.
A flag flew from the top of the mast.
The ship has three tall masts.

easy.def: Someone who is very good at something.
examples: He is a master painter.
The master carved the bowl.
He is a chess master.

more.def: A person who has great skill at something.
examples: The master baker made the wedding cake.
She is a master of the violin.
A master carver made the wooden horse.

easy.def: To learn something very well.
examples: I mastered tying my shoes.
She mastered the piano piece.
He mastered the trick.

more.def: To learn something so well that you can do it easily.
examples: It took a year to master the violin.
She mastered riding a bike without help.
He mastered the card trick after hours of practice.

easy.def: A very clever person who plans things.
examples: The mastermind made a plan.
A clever mastermind.
The mastermind of the show.

more.def: A very clever person who plans and directs a big project.
examples: The mastermind behind the play wrote the script and designed the sets.
The detective searched for the mastermind of the plan.
She was the mastermind of the school fair.

easy.def: A work of art that is very, very good.
examples: The painting is a masterpiece.
Her song was a masterpiece.
The cake was a masterpiece.

more.def: A work of art, music or writing that is among the best ever made.
examples: The painting is a masterpiece that hangs in a famous museum.
Her song was a masterpiece, and everyone loved it.
The cake was a sweet masterpiece, with flowers made of icing.

easy.def: Being very good at something.
examples: She showed mastery.
His mastery of chess is great.
She works for mastery.

more.def: Great skill in or complete knowledge of something.
examples: She showed mastery of the violin.
His mastery of chess won him the title.
The class worked toward mastery of times tables.

easy.def: A flat piece that lies on the floor.
examples: Wipe your feet on the mat.
The cat sleeps on a mat.
We sat on a yoga mat.

more.def: A flat piece of material that you put on the floor to sit on, stand on or protect it.
examples: Wipe your shoes on the mat before you come in.
The gym class did rolls on a soft mat.
A cork mat under the hot pan protected the table.

easy.def: A thin stick that makes fire.
examples: A grown-up lit a match.
The match went out.
The box of matches is on the shelf.

more.def: A small stick with a tip that makes a flame when rubbed on a rough surface.
examples: Dad struck a match to light the candle.
A box of matches sat on the shelf.
He blew out the match.

easy.def: A game between teams.
examples: We watched the soccer match.
The tennis match was long.
My dad won his tennis match.

more.def: A contest between two players or teams.
examples: The tennis match lasted two hours.
Our team won the match.
She watched the chess match.

easy.def: To go together.
examples: The socks match.
Her shoes match her dress.
These two colors match.

more.def: To be alike or to go well together.
examples: Her scarf matches her hat.
Match each word with its picture.
The two socks match.

related.def: Things that do not go together.

easy.def: A small paper folder with matches.
examples: The matchbook was on the table.
I found a matchbook.
The matchbook is small.

more.def: A small folded paper cover holding a row of matches.
examples: A matchbook sat on the old table.
He saved a matchbook from the restaurant.
Never play with a matchbook, because matches are dangerous.

easy.def: A small box that holds matches.
examples: The matchbox is empty.
A matchbox is small.
The matchbox is on the shelf.

more.def: A small box in which matches are kept.
examples: The matchbox was kept on a high shelf away from the children.
A tiny toy car fit inside the matchbox.
He used an empty matchbox as a bed for his toy mouse.

easy.def: Alike or going together.
examples: We wore matching hats.
I need a matching sock.
They have matching bikes.

more.def: Looking the same or going well together.
examples: The twins wore matching red coats.
She found a matching sock under the bed.
A game of matching cards tests your memory.

easy.def: The wooden stick of a match.
examples: He built with matchsticks.
The matchstick is thin.
A burnt matchstick.

more.def: The small stick of a match.
examples: He built a tiny house out of matchsticks.
The matchstick was thin and short.
Artists sometimes make models from matchsticks.

easy.def: A friend or partner.
examples: My mate and I play.
The ship's mate.
A classmate.

more.def: A friend or a partner, or a person you share something with.
examples: My teammate and I passed the ball.
The ship's mate told the crew what to do.
My roommate and I share a room.

easy.def: An animal's partner.
examples: The bird found a mate.
Wolves have one mate.
The swan stays with its mate.

more.def: One of a pair of animals that come together to have young.
examples: The bird sang to find a mate.
Swans stay with the same mate for life.
The wolf stayed close to its mate.

easy.def: What something is made from.
examples: Wood is a good material for a house.
The dress is made of soft material.
Glass is a hard material.

more.def: Any substance that things can be made from, or the cloth used to make clothes.
examples: Brick is a strong material for building houses.
She bought blue material to sew a new curtain.
The art teacher gave us paper and other materials to make a puppet.

easy.def: To appear or come to be real.
examples: The ghost will materialize.
The plan materialized.
A bus materialized.

more.def: To appear suddenly, or to become real.
examples: A bus finally materialized out of the fog.
The magician made a flower materialize.
The plan to build a park never materialized.

easy.def: The study of numbers and shapes.
examples: I like math.
We do math at school.
Math class is fun.

more.def: The subject in which you learn about numbers, shapes and measuring.
examples: We do math every morning at school.
She is good at math.
I use math to count my money.

easy.def: Having to do with math.
examples: A mathematical problem.
She has mathematical skill.
The mathematical idea.

more.def: Having to do with mathematics, or exact like math.
examples: She solved the mathematical problem on the board.
The engineer made a mathematical plan for the bridge.
He has a mathematical mind and loves number puzzles.

easy.def: A person who is an expert at math.
examples: A mathematician solves numbers.
The mathematician wrote on the board.
My aunt is a mathematician.

more.def: A person who is an expert in math and studies numbers and shapes.
examples: The mathematician solved a hard puzzle with numbers.
A famous mathematician came to visit our school.
Mathematicians study patterns in numbers and shapes.

easy.def: The study of numbers and shapes.
examples: We study mathematics at school.
Mathematics is fun.
She is good at mathematics.

more.def: The study of numbers, shapes and amounts, which includes adding, subtracting, multiplying and measuring.
examples: In mathematics class we learned how to find the area of a rectangle.
Mathematics helps builders measure and plan a house.
She loves mathematics because she likes solving number puzzles.

easy.def: A show or movie in the afternoon.
examples: We saw a matinee on Saturday.
The matinee starts at two.
Grandma took us to a matinee.

more.def: A play or movie shown in the daytime, usually in the afternoon.
examples: Tickets for the matinee cost less than for the evening show.
We went to the Sunday matinee of the school play.
The matinee ended in time for dinner.

easy.def: The state of being married.
examples: They joined in matrimony.
The pair were united in matrimony.
They lived in matrimony.

more.def: The state of being married, or the ceremony of marrying.
examples: The couple were joined in matrimony in a small ceremony in the garden.
The old story ends with a happy matrimony.
They lived in matrimony for fifty years.

easy.def: To be important.
examples: You matter to me.
It does not matter.
What matters is being kind.

more.def: To be important or to make a difference.
examples: It does not matter who wins, as long as we have fun.
Your opinion matters to our class.
Good sleep matters when you are growing.

easy.def: What things are made of.
examples: Rock is a kind of matter.
Water is matter.
Air is matter too.

more.def: Anything that takes up space and has weight, such as solids, liquids, and gases.
examples: Rocks, water, and air are all kinds of matter.
Matter can change from ice to water to steam.
Scientists study how matter behaves when it is heated.

easy.def: The soft part of a bed.
examples: The mattress is soft.
I jumped on the mattress.
The mattress is new.

more.def: The thick, soft pad that you lie on in a bed.
examples: The mattress is soft and thick.
We flipped the mattress over.
The cat slept on the mattress.

easy.def: Fully grown.
examples: The mature tree is tall.
A mature dog is calm.
The mature fruit is ripe.

more.def: Fully grown or developed, and acting in a sensible way.
examples: The mature oak tree gave a lot of shade.
She is mature for her age.
A mature cat usually sleeps more than a kitten.

easy.def: Being fully grown or acting grown-up.
examples: She showed maturity.
The plant reached maturity.
Maturity takes time.

more.def: The state of being fully grown, or the ability to behave in a sensible, grown-up way.
examples: She showed maturity by taking care of her little brother.
The tree reached maturity after twenty years.
Maturity means thinking before you act.

easy.def: A light purple color.
examples: The scarf is mauve.
Mauve is light purple.
A mauve flower.

more.def: A pale, soft purple color.
examples: The sky turned mauve at dusk.
She wore a mauve scarf.
The walls were painted a soft mauve.

easy.def: The mouth of a big animal.
examples: The lion's maw was wide.
The whale opened its maw.
The maw was big.

more.def: The mouth and throat of a large animal, or any wide opening.
examples: The lion opened its huge maw and roared.
The cave's dark maw loomed ahead.
The whale's maw was wide.

easy.def: A short saying that gives good advice.
examples: "Look before you leap" is a maxim.
The maxim is wise.
A famous maxim.

more.def: A short saying that expresses a useful truth or rule.
examples: "Look before you leap" is an old maxim.
The teacher wrote a maxim on the board.
My grandmother lives by the maxim "Be kind."

easy.def: To make as big as you can.
examples: She wants to maximize the fun.
We maximize our time.
He maximized the window.

more.def: To make something as large or as great as possible.
examples: We want to maximize our time at the park.
He maximized the window to fill the whole screen.

easy.def: The most you can have.
examples: The maximum is ten.
The maximum speed is fifty.
The elevator has a maximum of eight people.

more.def: The greatest amount or number that is allowed or possible.
examples: The bag can hold a maximum of ten pounds.
The maximum speed here is thirty miles per hour.
The jar holds a maximum of one quart.

easy.def: A word used to ask or say what is allowed.
examples: May I go out?
You may sit here.
May I have some?

more.def: A word used to ask for permission, or to say that something is possible.
examples: May I borrow your ruler for a minute?
It may rain later, so take an umbrella.
You may leave the table when you have finished eating.

easy.def: Not sure, but it may be.
examples: Maybe it will rain.
Maybe I can come.
Maybe she is home.

more.def: Possibly, or perhaps, when you are not sure.
examples: Maybe we can go to the park if the rain stops.
I am not sure, but maybe my sister took it.
Maybe the answer is on the next page.

easy.def: A call for help from a ship or plane.
examples: The pilot called mayday.
The captain shouted "Mayday!"
The mayday was heard.

more.def: A word shouted on the radio by a ship or plane in great trouble.
examples: The pilot radioed "Mayday!" when the engine failed.
The captain called mayday as the ship tilted.
The rescue boat heard the mayday call.

easy.def: The ship that brought the Pilgrims to America.
examples: The Mayflower crossed the sea.
We read about the Mayflower.
The Pilgrims sailed on the Mayflower.

more.def: The ship that carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620.
examples: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims across the Atlantic Ocean in 1620.
We built a model of the Mayflower in class.
The voyage of the Mayflower took more than two months.

easy.def: A wild, noisy mess.

more.def: A state of wild confusion, noise and disorder.
examples: Mayhem broke out in the kitchen when the pot boiled over.
The puppies caused mayhem by chasing each other through the house.

easy.def: A creamy white sauce for sandwiches.

We use mayonnaise in the salad.

more.def: A thick, creamy, pale sauce made from eggs and oil that is spread on sandwiches or mixed into salads.
examples: Dad spread mayonnaise on the bread for the sandwiches.

easy.def: The leader of a city or town.
examples: The mayor spoke.

more.def: The leader of a city or town, chosen by the people who live there.
examples: The mayor cut the ribbon at the new park.
Our mayor visited the school.
The mayor gave a speech at the parade.

easy.def: A puzzle of paths where you try to find the way out.
examples: I walked through the maze.
The maze was hard.
We drew a maze.

more.def: A set of paths with many turns and dead ends, where you try to find your way to the middle or the way out.
examples: We got lost in the corn maze for half an hour before we found the exit.
